topic: How does the 14.6% bandwidth affect frequency planning for multi-satellite networks with adjacent channel interference risks?
consensus_response: The 14.6% bandwidth significantly affects frequency planning in multi-satellite networks, increasing adjacent channel interference risks due to insufficient frequency separation between channels. To mitigate these issues, dynamic frequency selection (DFS), adaptive modulation and coding (AMC), and interference cancellation techniques can be employed. Additionally, optimizing satellite spacing, using digital predistortion (DPD) or envelope elimination and restoration (EER) techniques, and employing advanced linearization techniques like DPD or EER can help reduce non-linear effects and noise floor contributions. Furthermore, dynamic spectrum access (DSA) and cognitive radio networks (CRN) enable flexible frequency allocation to balance trade-offs between available bandwidth and adjacent channel interference risks.
